text.content:
Sect: Sabbat (revenant family)

Patron Clan: Tzimisce

Aristocrats of the social scene, the Zantosas care little for raw power or money beyond what sustains their lifestyle. Their professed purpose is to push the boundaries of human experience as far as they will go, chasing ever-fresh sensation and setting trends others imitate. The family is concentrated in Eastern Europe and spread across the Atlantic, with some Toreador antitribu treating them as kindred spirits, some Ventrue antitribu finding them decadent but useful, and the Serpents of the Light recently drawn into close cultural and religious association with them.

Role: Hedonists, trendsetters, and social manipulators whose excesses (and occasional scandals — blackmail, addiction, worse) keep mortal high society stirred up and entangled with Sabbat interests.

A hidden thread runs beneath the decadence: family elders have for generations guarded the deeply torpid body of a Tzimisce elder, brought to New York by the first sizable Zantosa contingent there. The body vanished without warning; a wave of mysterious deaths among elders who tended it followed. The family's cover story — periodic public purges of supposed Zantosa infernalist cells, which the Sabbat Inquisition has so far accepted at face value — is actually misdirection for these unexplained killings, and no one outside the inner circle knows the truth.

Disciplines: Auspex, Presence, Vicissitude

Weakness: No Zantosa is trained to resist temptation. Whenever a Zantosa encounters what looks like an intense, interesting pleasure, she must win a Self-Control or Instinct test (typically against a difficulty of three Traits) or abandon what she was doing to chase it instead; Zantosas cannot spend Willpower to resist supernatural enticements that carry any pleasurable component.

Path: Most follow the Path of Cathari, with a sizable minority on the Path of Death and the Soul, and at least one rural enclave (closely tied to the Bratovitches) on the Path of the Feral Heart. No Zantosa openly admits to the Path of Caine, despite persistent rumors of Noddists in the family.
